project: Road tanker braking and internal partition comparison
user_direction: Baseline -> one or two principle-demonstrating improvements -> a current commercial-style arrangement. Render actual SPH liquid inside a translucent tanker on a truck following a consistent prescribed road/braking trajectory; keep the fluid problem simple.
audience_question: The truck stops. What happens to the liquid inside?
initial_objective: Show how internal layout changes liquid motion and the timing/distribution of loads during and after an identical braking input.

cases.description: One continuous liquid space with no internal plate.
Two liquid-tight transverse bulkheads create three independent liquid compartments. Each gas space is assumed vented to atmospheric pressure; this is not a compressed-gas sealed-vessel model.
Two transverse plates at x=-1,+1m, each with four480mm-diameter resolved openings.

Perforated transverse plates plus a longitudinal baffle in the same outer tank. A simplified arrangement inspired by current commercial water-truck designs; exact proprietary geometry has not been obtained.
cases.role: Current commercial-style design; not a claim of newest invention or universally best performance.

fixed: Dry vehicle mass 9000 kg, CG and inertia
Gravity, contact friction and numerical settings
fair_comparison.fill_policy: Adjust the initial level for solid displacement so total liquid mass matches. For the compartmented case use balanced loading, with the same intended fill fraction across its compartments. Record generated particle masses and actual fill levels.
fair_comparison.effect_direction: Do not assume baffles minimize every peak. Compare actual total and local loads; added plates can transfer loads to other locations or times.
fair_comparison.structural_mass: Same hypothetical dry mass and inertia for all layouts; added baffle mass is not separately represented.
fair_comparison.commercial_model_note: Keep the outer tank envelope and CG placement fixed. Do not combine a lower commercial tank profile with extra baffles in one comparison and attribute all differences to baffles.

provisional_scenario.geometry: Cylindrical tank:6m length,1m inner radius. Two transverse plates at x=-1,+1m; perforated holes radius0.24m at y=+-0.42m,z=+-0.40m. D adds continuous longitudinal plate.
provisional_scenario.liquid: Water at approximately ambient conditions for the initial comparison, not fuel or LNG.
provisional_scenario.acceleration_profile: Smooth onset and release; integrate the prescribed tank acceleration to a consistent speed curve ending at zero. No step jump in acceleration solely to manufacture an impact.
provisional_scenario.observation: Include time after braking ends to show residual surge and load reversals.
provisional_scenario.status: Executed v8 setup; all four8s runs qualified.

numerical_approach.candidate_solver: Unmodified DualSPHysics5.4 numerical source, separate GPU/Chrono-enabled build.
numerical_approach.frame: Nonrotating accelerating support frame. Equal inertial acceleration applied to liquid and dry body. Native SPH/Chrono transfers fluid loads and freely solved body motion in both directions.
numerical_approach.local_capability_checked: work/DualSPHysics-source/doc/xml_format/_FmtXML_AccInput.xml provides time-dependent linear acceleration; retain gravity explicitly via globalgravity configuration.
numerical_approach.initial_relative_velocity: Zero after initial hydrostatic settling; displayed road speed is not injected as liquid velocity relative to the stationary tank.
numerical_approach.free_surface: Single liquid with atmospheric-pressure gas space; air compression, entrainment and ventilation dynamics are not resolved.
numerical_approach.motion_scope: Rigid body with six fixed wheel contact meshes and unilateral frictional road contact. No suspension, steering geometry, tire force curve or ABS. This is a support-platform surrogate, not a calibrated road-vehicle prediction.
numerical_approach.resolution: DP 40 mm; first resolution. 160 mm internal plates for moving-body compartment qualification. Same water particle count.
numerical_approach.force_extraction: Official ComputeForces boundary-particle vectors partitioned by initial particle IDs; whole-tank force/moment sums verified against native fluid-on-body records. Common0.4s smoothing for integrated loads.

presentation.primary_format: Portrait, short English labels; composition can later be adapted to landscape.
sequence: Boundary load contours and total force/moment arrows/numbers
presentation.truck_role: Truck rigid pose is solved by nativeSPH/Chrono. Road cues and INPUT SPEED are prescribed forward-reference speed, not solved total sliding velocity.
visuals: Translucent tank and real SPH liquid surface

presentation.interpretation: Full liquid momentum must still be removed during stopping. Baffles change load distribution and transient response; do not claim they remove the necessary braking impulse.
presentation.final_edit: Full rollover intro at2x. Particle count and fluid/rigid equations2.5s. Remove repeated implementation/caveat prose. Independent portrait/landscape compositions.

future_extensions: Vehicle suspension/tire calibration before real-vehicle safety claims

sources.use: Section 8.2 distinguishes liquid-tight bulkheads, perforated baffles and unbaffled tanks; longitudinal and lateral surge are different. Used for definitions, not a legal compliance claim.

sources.title: The Effect of Baffle Design on Longitudinal Liquid Movement in Road Tankers: An Experimental Investigation
sources.use: Experimental evidence that baffle arrangement influences braking-induced surge. Does not establish a universal best geometry or validate the proposed setup.
